📖 Reading: `C:\Users\mudas\AI-Disaster-Management-System\frontend\src\pages\Login.jsx`# AI Disaster Management System — Complete Feature & Process Analysis

## 1. What the project is

A full-stack **Enterprise Disaster Response Platform** for Government EOCs / disaster authorities / humanitarian orgs. It lets users report disasters and admins coordinate the entire response — AI damage prediction, live monitoring, rescue teams, route planning, hospitals/shelters/drones/resources, analytics and reporting.

Two apps run together:
- **Backend** — Java 17, Spring Boot 3.2, REST API on `:8080` + raw WebSocket on `/ws/live`, JPA/Hibernate over in-memory **H2** DB.
- **Frontend** — React 18 + Vite + **MUI** command-center UI on `:5173`, talks to backend via Vite proxy.

## 2. How a request flows through the system (step by step)

1. User opens `localhost:5173` → Vite dev server serves React.
2. User logs in → `AuthContext.login()` calls `POST /api/auth/login`.
3. Backend `AuthController` → `AuthService` authenticates against DB (BCrypt check) → `JwtUtils` generates a JWT token → returned as `{token, id, username, email, role}`.
4. Frontend stores it in `localStorage` (Remember Me) or `sessionStorage`; `api.js` axios interceptor attaches `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to every request.
5. Every subsequent request passes through `JwtAuthFilter` (SecurityConfig `src/main/java/com/disaster/config/SecurityConfig.java:46`) which validates the token and sets the authenticated user.
6. `SecurityConfig` guards endpoints by role: `/api/auth/**`, `/h2-console`, `/ws/**` are public; `/api/audit-logs/**`, `/api/exports/**`, `/api/admin/**` require `ADMIN`; everything else requires any authenticated user.
7. Controller → Service → Repository → H2 DB → JSON response → React page renders it. Frontend route protection (`ProtectedRoute.jsx`) redirects logged-out users to `/login` and non-admins away from `adminOnly` routes.

## 3. Backend modules (what each does)

**Auth & Security** — JWT (jjwt 0.12.3), BCrypt hashing, stateless sessions, CORS for the frontend origin, demo users seeded.

**Disaster module** — `DisasterService` (`DisasterService.java:36`) creates a disaster, then **chains 4 side-effects**: writes a `StatusTimeline` entry ("Disaster reported"), writes an **audit log**, creates an in-app **notification**, and fires **mock SMS + Email** alerts. `updateStatus` does the same for every status change (6-status lifecycle: PENDING → ASSIGNED → IN_PROGRESS → etc.).

**AI Engine** — `AIPredictionService` (`AIPredictionService.java:9`) is a rule-based predictor behind a `PredictionEngine` interface (swappable with real ML later). It computes: damage level, affected population, economic loss (₹), recovery time, **priority score, risk score, confidence %, response time**, plus a natural-language recommendation. `ResourceOptimizationService` computes a full resource allocation plan (ambulances, boats, helicopters, medical teams…) based on disaster type × severity.

**Real-time** — `WebSocketConfig` (`WebSocketConfig.java:16`) keeps a list of open sessions at `/ws/live`; `broadcastUpdate(type, data)` serializes a `LiveUpdateDTO` and pushes JSON to every connected client (types: `DISASTER`, `NOTIFICATION`, `DRONE_LOCATION`, `RESOURCE_LOCATION`, `VOLUNTEER_LOCATION`, `DASHBOARD`). Drone GPS positions auto-simulate and broadcast.

**Rescue Teams** — full CRUD + assign team↔disaster, 6 team statuses, member management (leaders/medics), equipment & vehicle tracking.

**Route Optimization** — `RouteOptimizationService` (`RouteOptimizationService.java:14`) uses the **Haversine formula** (offline, no API) to compute total distance/time, supports **multi-destination waypoints**, and returns a polyline for the Leaflet map.

**Case Studies** — `CaseStudyServiceImpl` stores historical disasters with lessons-learned; supports search by year/type/location and **statistical comparison** (avg damage, population, response/recovery time) for charts.

**Admin Center** — `AdminController` aggregates dashboard metrics (users, disasters, teams, pending, active missions, uptime), exposes editable **system settings** and a **health endpoint**.

**Entity CRUD + Services** — Hospitals, Shelters, Volunteers, Resources, Drones (full create/read/update/delete). Plus: **Notifications** (unread badge), **Audit Logs**, **Analytics** (12+ metrics, 4 chart types), **Exports** (CSV/TXT/PDF via OpenCSV), **Weather** (mock provider).

**DataSeeder** (`DataSeeder.java:51`) — runs on first boot; seeds 2 users, 4 disasters, 3 hospitals/shelters/volunteers, 5 resources, 3 drones, 3 rescue teams + members, 2 case studies, 3 system settings. Login defaults: **admin/admin123**, **user/user123**.

## 4. Frontend structure & UX

**Routing** (`App.jsx`) — 22 pages; every page wrapped in `ProtectedRoute`; admin pages (`adminOnly`) redirect non-admins. Includes 404 page.

**Shared components** — MUI `Sidebar` (dark command-center nav; shows an extra collapsible **Administration** section only for admins), `NotificationBell` (unread count), `WebSocketStatus` (green/red live chip), `AnimatedCounter`, `LoadingSkeleton`, `EmptyState`, `Breadcrumbs`, `ErrorBoundary`, `Footer`.

**Contexts** — `AuthContext` (login/register/logout/demo-login, remember-me storage) and `WebSocketContext` (`WebSocketContext.jsx:12`) which auto-connects, **auto-reconnects every 5s on drop**, parses JSON, and routes messages to subscribers by type (so pages get live disaster/notification/drone updates).

## 5. USER workflow (citizen/reporter)

1. **Register** or click **User Demo** → lands on `UserDashboard`.
2. **Report Disaster** — pick type (8: Flood/Earthquake/Cyclone/Wildfire/Tsunami/Landslide/Drought/Epidemic), severity (4), location, description → backend returns AI prediction + resource recommendations live.
3. **My Disasters** — see reported disasters; each gets in-app notification + mock SMS/email.
4. **AI Insights** — run predictions/recommendations on-demand; **Route Planner** — plan rescue routes; **Case Studies** — read historical lessons.
5. **Live Map** — OSM with street/terrain/satellite layers, color-coded disaster markers.
6. **Notifications & Profile** — view alerts, edit own profile, change own password.

## 6. ADMIN workflow (coordinator)

Everything a user can do **plus**:
1. **All Disasters** — view/search everything; **update status** (drives timeline, audit, notifications); delete.
2. **Users** — CRUD, search/filter, change roles, activate/deactivate, reset passwords, view activity.
3. **Rescue Teams** — create teams, add members, **assign to disasters**, track status.
4. **Drones / Hospitals / Shelters / Volunteers / Resources** — full management CRUD; drones show live simulated GPS.
5. **Audit Logs** — full activity trail; **Analytics** — monthly trends, type/severity/status charts, utilization %, averages.
6. **Exports** — download CSV/TXT/PDF reports.
7. **Control Center** — aggregated dashboard, system health/uptime, editable settings (system name, version, maintenance mode).

## 7. Key design notes

- **Graceful degradation**: UI keeps working if WebSocket drops.
- **Role-based access enforced on BOTH sides**: backend `SecurityConfig`/`@PreAuthorize` + frontend `ProtectedRoute`/conditional sidebar.
- **Audit + Timeline**: every disaster mutation leaves a trace (who, when, from→to status).
- **Mock providers** (SMS/Email/Weather) are interface-based — ready to swap for Twilio/Spring Mail/OpenWeatherMap.
- AI prediction & route calculation are **rule/geo-formula based** (no external API), behind interfaces for future ML/OSM integration.

**Total surface**: 21 backend controllers, 16 entities, 31 services, 26+ DTOs, 22 React pages, 11 shared components.
